# Prospective autonomous AI-review amendment v0.1

Status: **frozen prospective methodological amendment; not executed**

Amendment identity:
`candidate-screening-v0.2.0-prospective-autonomous-ai-review-v0.1`

Exact base commit:
`7c6acd7ffe73d020ffd3e3b70590f4f27dc77ee3`

Effective position: **22**

## Explicit protocol-phase split

Positions 1–21 are immutable historical production under
`candidate-screening-v0.2.0` and its original reviewer-authority regime.
Position 21 terminally published as `OUT_OF_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED`. This amendment
does not relabel, reinterpret, or change any historical decision or artifact.

Before Position 22 was opened, reviewer authority was prospectively changed
for operational reasons. Position 22 onward uses an authoritative non-human
`AI_FIRST_REVIEW` for every `STRUCTURED_REVIEW_REQUIRED` case. When the
unchanged frozen Reviewer B trigger requires a second review, another fresh,
independently blinded non-human `AI_SECOND_REVIEW` is authoritative.

This authority change is not claimed to be scientifically neutral. It creates
a protocol-phase difference between historical Positions 1–21 and amended
Positions 22 onward and is a methodological limitation when interpreting or
comparing outcomes across the phases. Candidate order and the evidence made
available to each logical review role do not change.

## Unchanged scientific authority

The amendment changes only ordinary semantic reviewer authority and the
minimal assignment/decision provenance needed to represent it honestly. It
does not amend the frozen candidate universe, sealed queue or order,
administrative exclusions, repository-anchor limits, global anchor accounting,
G0/G1 automatic authority, G2–G8 extraction semantics, TPTM implementation,
hybrid routing, Q1–Q10, `YES`/`NO`/`UNKNOWN` semantics, affirmative-evidence
requirements, trust or witness ontology, source condition, Reviewer B trigger,
Reviewer B blinding, disagreement handling, family feasibility/construction,
exact focal-hypothesis requirement, executable validation, repository
independence, category limits, stopping rule, or 1,000-anchor ceiling.

In particular, insufficient evidence remains `UNKNOWN`; absence of evidence is
not evidence for `NO`. A source already violating the focal proposition does
not qualify. `REVIEW_UNRESOLVED` may use only the frozen constrained
family-feasibility route, and no controller may synthesize a unique focal
hypothesis.

Final admission still requires every executable equivalent of:

```text
p*(S)=TRUE
p*(C)=TRUE
p*(I)=FALSE
required functional oracle(s)=PASS
reuse witness=TRIGGERED
safe witness=BLOCKED
exactly_one_focal_trust_change=TRUE
trust_category=KNOWN
repository_independence=PASS
```

AI judgment cannot override executable validation.

## Fresh one-shot roles and provenance

Every logical role uses a new `codex exec` operating-system process. Neither
`codex resume` nor `codex fork` is permitted. At minimum, a structured-review
position uses separate Position controller, `AI_FIRST_REVIEW`, continuation,
`AI_SECOND_REVIEW` when triggered, and combination/continuation processes.
The next position, after terminal publication only, starts another process.

AI semantic output is mechanically validated against the unchanged frozen
Q1–Q10 types and outcome derivation. The canonical amended decision envelope
records non-human reviewer type and role, assignment and packet hashes, prompt
hash, decision hash, timestamps, installed Codex CLI version, configured or
observed model identifier when available, runner invocation identity, and the
fresh Codex thread identity when exposed by the CLI. Missing optional CLI
metadata is recorded as unavailable; it is never fabricated.
The frozen runner selector is `gpt-5.6-sol` with no named CLI profile; every
role command passes that model selector explicitly.

The amended envelope is authoritative prospectively. Its
`semantic_projection_sha256` binds the unchanged finite semantic fields using
the existing canonical TPTM representation; this internal compatibility
projection does not convert the AI role into a human role.

## Reviewer B blinding

Reviewer B runs in a separate bubblewrap filesystem capsule. The capsule
contains only the latest append-only, repository-authorized blinded assignment,
its hash-verified permitted evidence, and frozen interface files. The
production worktree, other position records, AI Reviewer A material, combined
state, outcomes, admission state, scores/gold, future queue material, Track B,
and Codex conversation history are not mounted. Assignment correction, when
needed, is append-only and numbered; an earlier assignment is never edited.

Any disagreement on a required answer or exact focal hypothesis yields
`REVIEW_UNRESOLVED`. There is no vote, reviewer priority, confidence weighting,
third reviewer, controller tie-break, or informal override.

## External unattended runner

The hash-bound runner is operational infrastructure outside this worktree at:

```text
/home/anjum/track-a-production-runner/
```

It holds one exclusive Track A `flock`, verifies the expected branch/HEAD and
tracked/index baseline, validates protocol/amendment/queue/ledger hashes,
replays every published record, launches role-specific one-shot processes,
and reads only durable orchestration metadata. It never performs semantic
candidate review. Logs and mutable expected-HEAD state remain outside Git.

The runner stops successfully on the unchanged global stopping rule or its
operational `--max-positions` bound. It fails closed on scientific or unresolved
engineering blockers, `ANALYSIS_ERROR`, integrity/replay/HEAD/blinding/decision
failures, ambiguous partial publication, future-position isolation violations,
missing frozen interfaces, or any state it cannot affirmatively prove safe.
Only a failed role proven to have made no durable change may be retried, and
the retry is another new process.

## Freeze boundary

At adoption the ledger has exactly 21 published/processed positions, two
historical unique opened anchors, 19 global unique opened anchors, no final
family or represented category, `next_due_position=22`, and
`global_action=CONTINUE`. Position 22 authorization, runtime directory, and
record are absent. This amendment and runner were frozen without resolving the
Position 22 queue entry, inspecting its candidate content, launching Codex for
production, or opening Position 22.

# Durable autonomous orchestration amendment v0.1

This append-only engineering amendment supplies the deterministic position
materialization interface that was missing at the Position 22 boundary and
supersedes only the external orchestration implementation. It does not rewrite
the Position 22 blocker, Positions 1–21, either predecessor amendment, the
sealed queue, TPTM, review semantics, family methodology, executable authority,
or the stopping rule.

Position 22 remains governed by the already-effective prospective autonomous
AI-review regime. The existing `MISSING_FROZEN_INTERFACE` blocker is immutable
historical evidence. A real runner invocation will validate it, mechanically
materialize Position 22 authorization and candidate manifest from the replayed
ledger, sealed queue, frozen discovery provenance, and immutable Git objects,
append a recovery receipt, commit those new files, and continue after that
boundary. This implementation/freeze session does not invoke that recovery.

The external v0.2 runner is a durable-state reconciler. It records role exits as
`ROLE_COMPLETED`, then independently validates HEAD ancestry, ledger checksum,
the full record replay, and exact current-position metadata before choosing a
next role. Codex prose has no transition authority. `AUTO_CONTINUE` is emitted
only after one terminal record and its one-position ledger transition validate.

The versioned transition matrix, deterministic recovery registry, and 67-item
test coverage manifest are frozen external artifacts. The runner also supplies
atomic heartbeat/state writes, child-PID watchdog reporting, restart recovery,
and read-only `--status`, `--events`, and `--doctor` commands.

The frozen validation boundary comprises 34 deterministic-materialization
tests, 109 durable v0.2 runner tests, and 144 combined legacy/v0.2 runner tests.

Scientific methodology is unchanged.

It defines the minimum quality gates every\nnew or modified workflow-called script must meet, and lists optional\nenhancements that may be added when the script's blast radius or\nexternal coupling warrants them.\n\nPer [CLAUDE.md](../CLAUDE.md) section 3, deterministic harness work\nbelongs in hooks and CI rather than reviewer memory; this standard is\nthe checklist a reviewer (human or agent) applies before a script\nlands. Per section 4, the must-have list never strips a check that\nprevents harm: dry-run defaults, secret handling, input validation,\nand loud failure are all encoded as must-have items.\n\n## Scope\n\nA \"workflow-called script\" is any Python module under `scripts/` that\nsatisfies all of the following:\n\n- It is invoked from at least one workflow under `.github/workflows/`\n  via `python3 scripts/<name>.py ...`.\n- It has a stable CLI contract (subcommands, flags, env vars) that the\n  workflow YAML depends on.\n- It may read repository state (files, GitHub API) and may produce\n  side effects: GitHub API writes, status annotations, summary output,\n  issue comments, or local file changes consumed downstream.\n\nShared library modules under `scripts/` whose name starts with an\nunderscore (`scripts/_github_api.py`, `scripts/_trusted_bots.py`) are\nnot workflow entry points and are not directly in scope. They should\nnevertheless meet the same testing and validation expectations,\nbecause the entry-point scripts inherit their behaviour.\n\nOut of scope for this document:\n\n- Shell-only workflow steps that do not call a Python module.\n- Local developer tooling that is never invoked by a workflow.\n- The `.apm/instructions/` source-of-truth tree, which has its own\n  compilation contract.\n\n## SoT layout\n\n| File | Target | Purpose |\n|---|---|---|\n| `docs/workflow-script-quality.md` *(this file)* | - | Standard runbook |\n| `pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` | local + CI | `pythonpath = [\"scripts\"]`, `testpaths = [\"tests\"]` so test modules can `import <name>` directly |\n| `scripts/_github_api.py` | shared library | Reusable HTTP boundary with retry and `Authorization: Bearer` handling |\n| `scripts/_trusted_bots.py` | shared library | Single source of truth for the trusted-bot allowlist |\n| `.github/workflows/verify-*.yml` | GitHub Actions | Read-only gate invocations (representative pattern) |\n| `.github/workflows/apply-*.yml` | GitHub Actions | Write-side dispatch invocations with `dry_run` input (representative pattern) |\n\n## Must-have checks\n\nEvery new or modified workflow-called script must satisfy each item\nbelow before merge. These are gates, not suggestions: if an item is\nintentionally skipped, the PR body must record why.\n\n### M1. Module shape: pure functions on top, thin IO boundary at the bottom\n\nLogic lives in pure functions that take primitive or dataclass inputs\nand return primitive or dataclass outputs. The only side-effecting\nsurface is a single `main(argv)` function plus, at most, one\nsubprocess or HTTP boundary helper. Tests monkeypatch the boundary;\nthey do not need to monkeypatch the logic.\n\nReference implementation: `scripts/scan_non_ascii.py` follows the\npattern documented in its module docstring; `scripts/uv_pin.py` is the\nprior art that pattern was extracted from.\n\n### M2. Unit tests under `tests/test_<name>.py`\n\nEvery workflow-called script has a matching test module. `pytest -q`\nfrom the repository root must exit 0. Tests exercise pure functions\ndirectly; tests for the boundary use monkeypatch to inject fakes.\n\nThe `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` block in `pyproject.toml` already sets\n`pythonpath = [\"scripts\"]` and `testpaths = [\"tests\"]`, so a test\nmodule simply imports the script by basename:\n\n```python\nimport issue_link\n```\n\n### M3. CLI contract tests\n\nThe argparse subcommand surface, required and optional flags, and\nenvironment-variable fallbacks are locked by tests that exercise\n`main(argv)` directly (or `subprocess.run` for end-to-end coverage of\nexit codes). The workflow YAML invocation is part of the contract; if\nthe YAML calls `--body-file` and falls back to `PR_BODY`, both paths\nmust have a test.\n\nReference: `tests/test_issue_link.py` covers both the body-file path\nand the env-var fallback path of `scripts/issue_link.py`.\n\n### M4. Input validation at boundaries\n\nEvery input that crosses the workflow-to-script boundary is validated\nbefore use. String booleans (`\"true\"` / `\"false\"`) are parsed with a\nhelper that rejects any other value. Numeric inputs are checked for\nsign and range. Enumerated inputs are checked against a `frozenset`\nallowlist. Unknown event types raise rather than producing an empty\nresult.\n\nReference: `scripts/branch_cleanup.py` `parse_dry_run` and\n`parse_min_age_days` reject malformed inputs with `ValueError`;\n`scripts/preflight_non_ascii.py` `_TARGET_TOOLS` is a `frozenset`\nallowlist.\n\n### M5. GitHub output and summary contracts\n\nScripts that need to surface results to GitHub Actions use the\ndocumented contracts, not ad-hoc stdout parsing:\n\n- Step summary: `--summary-file \"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\"` (the script\n  writes Markdown to the path the runner provides).\n- Step outputs: `--github-output \"$GITHUB_OUTPUT\"` (the script\n  appends `name=value` lines to the path the runner provides).\n- Errors: `::error::<message>` (and `::warning::`, `::notice::`) on\n  stdout, so the GitHub Actions UI surfaces them inline.\n\nReference: `.github/workflows/apply-rulesets.yml` passes\n`--summary-file \"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY\"`;\n`.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml` passes both\n`--github-output \"${GITHUB_OUTPUT}\"` and writes the step summary via\nshell redirection.\n\n### M6. Dry-run / plan-only default for mutating scripts\n\nAny script that can mutate GitHub state, repository files, or external\nsystems exposes a `--dry-run` mode (or equivalent plan-only\nsubcommand) and the workflow's `workflow_dispatch.inputs.dry_run`\ndefaults to `true`. The mutation path is enabled only by an explicit\n`dry_run=false` from a privileged dispatch.\n\nRead-only gates (the `verify-*.yml` family) do not need a dry-run\nmode; they are already non-mutating by construction.\n\nReference: `.github/workflows/apply-rulesets.yml` and\n`.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml` both default `dry_run` to\n`true`; `scripts/rulesets_apply.py` and `scripts/branch_cleanup.py`\nhonour the flag.\n\n### M7. Secret handling\n\nTokens and other secrets are read from environment variables, never\nfrom CLI arguments (which would leak into `ps` listings and into\nGitHub Actions step logs when echoed). The script does not print\nsecrets to stdout or stderr. HTTP calls funnel through\n`scripts/_github_api.py` so the `Authorization: Bearer <token>`\nheader is constructed in exactly one place.\n\nWorkflows guard required secrets with a loud `Guard <SECRET>` step\nthat exits 1 with `::error::` when the secret is unset. Reference:\nthe `Guard RULESETS_PAT` step in\n`.github/workflows/apply-rulesets.yml`.\n\n### M8. Lint, type, and coverage gates\n\nScripts are written so they pass the repository's lint, type, and\ncoverage gates when those gates land. Concretely:\n\n- Type hints on every public function signature and on every\n  non-trivial local variable.\n- No unused imports, no shadowed builtins, no bare `except:`.\n- Pure functions are individually testable so coverage threshold gates\n  can be met without integration tests.\n\nThe repository currently runs `pytest` as the only Python gate. Issue\n#192 tracks adding static lint and type checks; issue #188 tracks\nadding a coverage threshold. New scripts should be written so neither\nof those follow-ups requires reworking the script.\n\n### M9. Fail-loud vs fail-open policy\n\nEach script declares in its module docstring whether it is a gate\n(fails loud, exits non-zero on unexpected input) or a hook (fails\nopen, exits zero with an `::error::` annotation when input is\nmalformed so the hook never wedges the session).\n\n- Gates: `scripts/title_policy.py`, `scripts/issue_link.py`,\n  `scripts/scan_non_ascii.py`, `scripts/body_policy.py`.\n- Hooks: `scripts/preflight_non_ascii.py` (its docstring states\n  explicitly: \"Fails open per CLAUDE.md section 4: any parse error or\n  unexpected payload shape ... exits 0 with no decision\").\n\nPer CLAUDE.md section 4, \"when a check IS warranted, fail loudly\".\nThe hook exception exists only because a session-blocking hook bug\nwould be worse than the gate it backs up; the server-side gate\nremains as backstop.\n\n## Optional enhancements\n\nThe items below are not gates. Add them when the script's blast\nradius, external coupling, or historical bug pattern warrants the\nextra investment.\n\n### O1. Property-based or fuzz tests\n\nWhen the script parses user-authored prose or untrusted JSON, add\nproperty-based tests (e.g. Hypothesis) that exercise the parser on\ngenerated inputs. Consider this when the script has shipped a parser\nbug, or when the parser sits on an injection-relevant boundary.\n\n### O2. Fixture-driven external API tests\n\nWhen the script consumes an external API, add a `--<source>-file`\nflag that reads the same shape from disk so tests can run without\nnetwork access. Reference: `scripts/threat_intel_triage.py` exposes\n`--osv-file` and `--kev-file` for exactly this purpose.\n\n### O3. Workflow invocation drift verification\n\nWhen the workflow YAML and the script's argparse surface drift,\nsilent breakage results. A periodic check that parses the YAML and\nthe argparse spec and asserts they agree closes the loop. Tracked by\nissue #193.\n\n### O4. Coverage thresholds\n\nA per-module coverage floor catches regressions where new branches\nland without tests. Tracked by issue #188. Until that lands, aim for\n\"every pure function has at least one positive and one negative\ntest.\"\n\n### O5. Pydantic-based input modelling\n\nFor scripts that accept rich nested input (JSON event payloads, multi-\nfield configs), modelling the input with pydantic gives a single\ndeclarative validation surface and better error messages than hand-\nwritten `isinstance` checks. Tracked by issue #191.\n\n### O6. GitHub API boundary contract tests\n\nFor scripts that talk to the GitHub API, contract tests that record\nthe request shape (method, URL, headers, body keys) catch regressions\nwhen the boundary helper changes. Tracked by issue #194.\n\n### O7. Standardised dependency and tool installation\n\nWhen a script needs a third-party dependency, declare it in\n`pyproject.toml` so `uv sync` resolves it deterministically rather\nthan relying on ad-hoc `pip install` lines in workflow YAML. Tracked\nby issue #195.\n\n## Worked example: minimal script skeleton\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"<one-line purpose>.\n\nThe workflow `.github/workflows/<name>.yml` invokes this module.\n\nContract:\n- Inputs: <flag list and env-var fallbacks>.\n- Outputs: <stdout shape>, <summary file shape>, <exit codes>.\n- Failure policy: fails <loud|open> per CLAUDE.md section 4.\n\nTested by `tests/test_<name>.py`. It scans a local collection of Markdown, YAML, and JSON files\nand produces an inspectable inventory of artifacts such as agent definitions,\ncapability modules, prompt templates, tool manifests, schemas, and\nprotocol-facing manifests.\n\nThe project is intentionally small enough to inspect. Its source artifacts,\nschemas, generated outputs, diagnostics, tests, CI workflow, and safety\nboundaries are all visible in the repository.\n\n## Architecture direction\n\nThe current v0.3 showcase is CLI-first: it demonstrates the deterministic\nbackend that performs `catalog`, `validate`, and `report` actions. A future LLM\ninteraction layer can sit in front of this same backend to scope intent,\nexplain safety boundaries, propose bounded commands, ask for approval before\nexecution, and summarize the generated outputs.\n\nThat interaction layer would orchestrate the workflow, not replace the\ncataloging logic or invent findings. CLI-generated files remain the source of\ntruth for review. This distinction keeps the project precise about what is\nimplemented today and what is planned for a future agent-facing experience.\n\n## Why it exists\n\nAgentic systems depend on more than prompts. They also depend on artifacts that\ndescribe capabilities, activation conditions, inputs, outputs, tool access,\nside effects, dependencies, ownership, safety boundaries, and review status.\n\nThose artifacts need to be addressable, versionable, inspectable, and\ngovernable. `agent-librarian` demonstrates one practical way to inventory and\nreview them without requiring a hosted service or an autonomous model.\n\n## What it demonstrates\n\n- artifact-first agent system design\n- local-only scanning that treats selected files as data\n- deterministic generated outputs\n- schema-backed catalog validation\n- per-file parse diagnostics and strict mode\n- warning and overlap surfaces for human review\n- configurable scan include and exclude patterns\n- explicit public-safety boundaries\n- CI-backed validation and release hygiene\n- separation between source artifacts and generated review outputs\n\n## How it works at a glance\n\n```text\nlocal artifact collection\n  -> safe scanner and structured parsers\n  -> artifact classification and metadata normalization\n  -> parse diagnostics and review warnings\n  -> deterministic overlap scoring\n  -> generated catalog and reports\n  -> schema validation and human review\n```\n\nThe scanner does not import, source, evaluate, or execute scanned artifacts.\nNormal mode isolates individual parse failures and records them in diagnostics.\nStrict mode produces outputs when practical, then exits non-zero when a\nselected file failed to parse.\n\n## What it produces\n\nA catalog run writes four files under the selected output directory:\n\n- `index.json`: machine-readable entries and generation metadata\n- `catalog.md`: a human-readable inventory with review warnings\n- `overlap-report.json`: deterministic overlap candidates\n- `diagnostics.json`: per-file parse status, warnings, and sanitized errors\n\nThe `validate` command checks the generated JSON against bundled schemas.\nValidation confirms expected structure; it does not certify completeness,\nsemantic correctness, safety, or publication readiness.\n\n## What this is not\n\nIt is:\n\n- not a hosted marketplace\n- not a private registry\n- not an LLM-powered reviewer by default\n- not a semantic or vector search system\n- not an automatic merge or deduplication engine\n- not a safety or correctness certification system\n- not a tool that executes scanned artifacts\n- not a replacement for human review\n\nCurrent v0.3 behavior does not use an LLM and is not an LLM-powered autonomous\nagent. It is the deterministic backend for a planned two-layer architecture,\nnot an autonomous agent runtime. Warnings and overlap candidates are review\nprompts, not decisions, and a future model summary must not present them as\nsafety, completeness, approval, or publication-readiness certifications.\n\n## Why it matters for agentic AI artifacts\n\nThe broader Agentic AI Artifact Taxonomy thesis is that reliable agentic\nsystems need inspectable artifacts around model behavior: schemas,\ninstructions, capability definitions, tool contracts, outputs, diagnostics,\nvalidation checks, safety boundaries, and release discipline.\n\nThe point is not that every agent needs this exact tool. The point is that\nagentic systems need inspectable artifacts around them, and those artifacts\nneed consistent ways to be cataloged, validated, reviewed, and governed.\n`agent-librarian` makes that thesis concrete in a small repository.\n\n## Safe demo boundaries\n\nFor public demos, use only the public repository, the committed synthetic\nsample artifacts, and generated outputs from `examples/sample-collection`.\n\nDo not demo private collections, employer workflows, internal repositories,\nprivate prompts, real traces, memory or state snapshots, credentials, secrets,\nregulated or private data, or generated catalogs from non-public sources.\n\nLocal and deterministic processing reduces exposure, but it does not make\narbitrary source material safe to publish. Human review of source artifacts\nand generated outputs remains required.\n\n## Where to start\n\n1. Read the [project overview](../README.md).\n2. Review the [taxonomy-aligned architecture map](taxonomy-architecture-map.md).\n3. Follow the [five-minute demo walkthrough](demo-walkthrough.md).\n4. Review the committed outputs in\n   [`examples/generated-catalog`](../examples/generated-catalog/).\n8. It connects generic\nartifact classes from the Agentic AI Artifact Taxonomy to concrete files,\nruntime behavior, generated outputs, and review surfaces in this repository.\n\nThe files under `agent/` are design-time descriptions of the system's\nidentity, operating stance, capability, tools, prompts, memory boundary, state\nboundary, and governance. The executable CLI is implemented under\n`src/agent_librarian/`; it does not load the `agent/` documents as runtime\ninstructions.\n\n## System summary\n\n`agent-librarian` is a local deterministic CLI that scans selected Markdown,\nYAML, and JSON files as data, classifies artifacts, normalizes metadata, emits\ndiagnostics and warnings, identifies overlap candidates, writes generated\ncatalog outputs, and validates generated JSON against bundled schemas.\n\nIt does not call an LLM or network service, execute scanned artifacts, maintain\na user memory store, or preserve hidden runtime session state. It does not\nautomatically approve, merge, delete, rewrite, or publish artifacts. def validate_existing_materialization(
    repository_root: Path, *, expected_position: int | None = None
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate a due materialized pair without source fetch or semantic output."""

    repository_root = repository_root.resolve()
    authorization_source = repository_root / PRODUCTION_AUTHORIZATION_RELATIVE_PATH
    if sha256_file(authorization_source) != PRODUCTION_AUTHORIZATION_SHA256:
        raise MaterializationError(
            "PRODUCTION_AUTHORIZATION_MISMATCH", str(authorization_source)
        )
    _validate_administrative_amendment(repository_root)
    ledger, _records, state = _load_ledger(repository_root)
    position = state.next_due_position
    if expected_position is not None and position != expected_position:
        raise MaterializationError(
            "LEDGER_POSITION_MISMATCH", f"expected={expected_position},due={position}"
        )
    if state.global_action.value != "CONTINUE":
        raise MaterializationError("GLOBAL_STOP", state.global_action.value)
    entry, _limit = _due_queue_entry(repository_root, position)
    if entry.get("queue_position") != position:
        raise MaterializationError("QUEUE_POSITION_MISMATCH", str(position))
    candidate, source_record, source_root = _validated_discovery_record(
        repository_root, entry
    )
    resolved_source = _source_resolution(
        entry, candidate, source_record, source_root
    )
    root = repository_root / RUN_RELATIVE_PATH / "positions" / f"{position:08d}"
    authorization_path = root / "position-authorization.json"
    manifest_path = root / "candidate-manifest.json"
    authorization = _load_object(authorization_path)
    manifest = _load_object(manifest_path)
    future = position + 1
    authorization_keys = {
        "schema",
        "protocol_version",
        "screening_method_version",
        "production_authorization_sha256",
        "queue_position",
        "queue_entry_sha256",
        "candidate_id",
        "status",
        "issued_at_utc",
        "scope",
        "source_resolution",
        f"network_accessed_for_position_{position}_source_resolution",
        "experiment_accessed",
        "historically_opened",
        "global_unique_anchor_accounting",
        "reviewer_b_boundary",
        f"position_{future}_authorized",
        f"candidate_{future}_authorized",
    }
    source_keys = {
        "identity_resolution",
        "repository",
        "repository_identity",
        "pull_request_number",
        "pull_request_title",
        "base_commit",
        "head_commit",
        "base_tree",
        "head_tree",
        "topology",
        "git_diff_sha256",
    }
    source = authorization.get("source_resolution")
    expected_scope = [
        "TPTM_G0_G8_EVIDENCE_EXTRACTION",
        "FROZEN_HYBRID_ROUTING",
        "REVIEWER_A_IF_REQUIRED",
        "REVIEWER_B_BLINDED_HANDOFF_IF_REQUIRED",
        "CONSTRAINED_FAMILY_WORK_IF_AUTHORIZED_AND_NO_HANDOFF_REMAINS",
        f"POSITION_{position}_PUBLICATION_IF_TERMINAL",
    ]
    expected_source = {
        "identity_resolution": (
            "FROZEN_CANDIDATE_HASH_MATCH_AGAINST_IMMUTABLE_GIT_"
            "COMMIT_PARENT_TOPOLOGY"
        ),
        "repository": resolved_source.repository,
        "repository_identity": resolved_source.repository_identity,
        "pull_request_number": resolved_source.pull_request_number,
        "pull_request_title": resolved_source.pull_request_title,
        "base_commit": resolved_source.base_commit,
        "head_commit": resolved_source.head_commit,
        "base_tree": resolved_source.base_tree,
        "head_tree": resolved_source.head_tree,
        "topology": resolved_source.topology,
    }
    issued_at = authorization.get("issued_at_utc")
    try:
        canonical_issued_at = (
            datetime.fromisoformat(str(issued_at).replace("Z", "+00:00"))
            .astimezone(timezone.utc)
            .replace(microsecond=0)
            .isoformat()
            .replace("+00:00", "Z")
        )
    except ValueError:
        canonical_issued_at = None
    if (
        set(authorization) != authorization_keys
        or canonical_json_bytes(authorization) != authorization_path.read_bytes()
        or authorization.get("schema")
        != "candidate-screening-position-authorization-v0.2.0"
        or authorization.get("protocol_version") != PROTOCOL_VERSION
        or authorization.get("screening_method_version") != SCREENING_METHOD_VERSION
        or authorization.get("production_authorization_sha256")
        != ledger.get("production_authorization_sha256")
        or authorization.get("queue_position") != position
        or authorization.get("queue_entry_sha256") != canonical_sha256(entry)
        or authorization.get("candidate_id") != entry.get("candidate_identity")
        or authorization.get("status") != f"AUTHORIZED_POSITION_{position}_ONLY"
        or canonical_issued_at != issued_at
        or authorization.get("scope") != expected_scope
        or not isinstance(source, Mapping)
        or set(source) != source_keys
        or any(source.get(key) != value for key, value in expected_source.items())
        or not isinstance(source.get("git_diff_sha256"), str)
        or len(source["git_diff_sha256"]) != 64
        or any(character not in "0123456789abcdef" for character in source["git_diff_sha256"])
        or not isinstance(
            authorization.get(
                f"network_accessed_for_position_{position}_source_resolution"
            ),
            bool,
        )
        or authorization.get("experiment_accessed") is not False
        or authorization.get("historically_opened") is not False
        or authorization.get("global_unique_anchor_accounting")
        != "DERIVE_WITH_FROZEN_ADVANCE_LEDGER_POSITION"
        or authorization.get("reviewer_b_boundary")
        != "STOP_AFTER_DURABLE_BLINDED_HANDOFF_IF_REQUIRED"
        or authorization.get(f"position_{future}_authorized") is not False
        or authorization.get(f"candidate_{future}_authorized") is not False
    ):
        raise MaterializationError("POSITION_AUTHORIZATION_INVALID", str(position))
    manifest_keys = {
        "schema_version",
        "candidate_id",
        "queue_position",
        "repository",
        "repository_independence_group",
        "base_commit",
        "head_commit",
        "changed_files",
        "analysis_version",
        "evidence",
        "implementation_anchor_evidence_id",
        "patch_sha256",
        "candidate_manifest_sha256",
    }
    evidence = manifest.get("evidence")
    expected_evidence = {
        "evidence_id": f"position-{position}-authorization",
        "kind": "POSITION_SCOPED_PRODUCTION_AUTHORIZATION",
        "path": str(
            RUN_RELATIVE_PATH
            / "positions"
            / f"{position:08d}"
            / "position-authorization.json"
        ),
        "sha256": sha256_file(authorization_path),
    }
    changed_files = manifest.get("changed_files")
    g0 = evaluate_g0(manifest)
    if (
        set(manifest) != manifest_keys
        or canonical_json_bytes(manifest) != manifest_path.read_bytes()
        or manifest.get("schema_version") != "tptm-candidate-manifest-v1"
        or manifest.get("candidate_id") != authorization.get("candidate_id")
        or manifest.get("queue_position") != position
        or manifest.get("repository") != source.get("repository")
        or manifest.get("repository_independence_group")
        != repository_independence_group(resolved_source.repository_identity)
        or manifest.get("base_commit") != source.get("base_commit")
        or manifest.get("head_commit") != source.get("head_commit")
        or manifest.get("analysis_version") != "tptm-analysis-v1"
        or manifest.get("implementation_anchor_evidence_id") is not None
        or not isinstance(changed_files, list)
        or not changed_files
        or g0.candidate is None
        or evidence != [expected_evidence]
        or manifest.get("patch_sha256") != patch_sha256(changed_files)
        or manifest.get("candidate_manifest_sha256")
        != candidate_manifest_sha256(manifest)
    ):
        raise MaterializationError("CANDIDATE_MANIFEST_INVALID", str(position))
    blocker, _blocker_path, blocker_digest = _validate_blocker(root, position)
    recovery_path = root / "position-materialization-recovery.json"
    if blocker is not None:
        recovery = _load_object(recovery_path)
        outputs = recovery.get("outputs")
        trigger = recovery.get("trigger")
        recovery_keys = {
            "schema",
            "amendment_id",
            "queue_position",
            "trigger",
            "validated_starting_head",
            "operation",
            "outputs",
            "resume_boundary",
            "blocker_preserved_unchanged",
            "ledger_advanced",
            "terminal_record_published",
            "scientific_methodology_changed",
        }
        trigger_keys = {
            "blocker_path",
            "blocker_sha256",
            "blocker_schema",
            "blocker_class",
            "stage",
        }
        starting_head = recovery.get("validated_starting_head")
        ancestor = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", str(starting_head), "HEAD"],
            cwd=repository_root,
            stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            check=False,
        )
        if (
            set(recovery) != recovery_keys
            or recovery.get("schema") != RECOVERY_SCHEMA
            or recovery.get("amendment_id") != AMENDMENT_ID
            or recovery.get("queue_position") != position
            or not isinstance(trigger, Mapping)
            or set(trigger) != trigger_keys
            or trigger.get("blocker_path")
            != str(RUN_RELATIVE_PATH / "positions" / f"{position:08d}" / "autonomous-blocker.json")
            or trigger.get("blocker_sha256") != blocker_digest
            or trigger.get("blocker_schema") != BLOCKER_SCHEMA
            or trigger.get("blocker_class") != BLOCKER_CLASS
            or trigger.get("stage") != BLOCKER_STAGE
            or not isinstance(starting_head, str)
            or len(starting_head) != 40
            or any(character not in "0123456789abcdef" for character in starting_head)
            or ancestor.returncode != 0
            or recovery.get("operation") != MATERIALIZATION_SCHEMA
            or recovery.get("resume_boundary") != "TPTM_REQUIRED"
            or recovery.get("blocker_preserved_unchanged") is not True
            or recovery.get("ledger_advanced") is not False
            or recovery.get("terminal_record_published") is not False
            or recovery.get("scientific_methodology_changed") is not False
            or not isinstance(outputs, Mapping)
            or set(outputs)
            != {"position_authorization_sha256", "candidate_manifest_sha256"}
            or outputs.get("position_authorization_sha256")
            != sha256_file(authorization_path)
            or outputs.get("candidate_manifest_sha256") != sha256_file(manifest_path)
        ):
            raise MaterializationError("RECOVERY_RECEIPT_INVALID", str(position))
    elif recovery_path.exists():
        raise MaterializationError("UNEXPECTED_RECOVERY_RECEIPT", str(position))
    return {
        "schema": MATERIALIZATION_SCHEMA,
        "queue_position": position,
        "position_authorization_sha256": sha256_file(authorization_path),
        "candidate_manifest_sha256": sha256_file(manifest_path),
        "blocker_recovery": blocker is not None,
        "next_state": "TPTM_REQUIRED",
        "writes_performed": False,
    }


def materialize_due_position(
    repository_root: Path,
    *,
    expected_position: int | None = None,
    source_repository: Path | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    plan, temporary = prepare_materialization(
        repository_root,
        expected_position=expected_position,
        source_repository=source_repository,
    )
    try:
        return apply_materialization(plan)
    finally:
        if temporary is not None:
            temporary.cleanup()

def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Frozen G0-G8 TPTM evidence and high-recall hybrid routing"
    )
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="operation", required=True)

    analyze = subparsers.add_parser("analyze-manifest")
    analyze.add_argument("--candidate", type=Path, required=True)
    analyze.add_argument("--repository-path", type=Path)
    analyze.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
    analyze.add_argument("--run-envelope", type=Path, required=True)

    validate = subparsers.add_parser("validate-result")
    validate.add_argument("--result", type=Path, required=True)

    replay = subparsers.add_parser("replay")
    replay.add_argument("--candidate", type=Path, required=True)
    replay.add_argument("--repository-path", type=Path)
    replay.add_argument("--expected", type=Path)
    replay.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    replay.add_argument("--runs", type=int, default=3)

    build_packet = subparsers.add_parser("build-review-packet")
    build_packet.add_argument("--result", type=Path, required=True)
    build_packet.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)

    validate_packet = subparsers.add_parser("validate-review-packet")
    validate_packet.add_argument("--packet", type=Path, required=True)

    validate_decision = subparsers.add_parser("validate-review-decision")
    validate_decision.add_argument("--decision", type=Path, required=True)
    validate_decision.add_argument("--review-packet", type=Path, required=True)

    route = subparsers.add_parser("hybrid-route")
    route.add_argument("--result", type=Path, required=True)
    route.add_argument("--output", type=Path)

    hybrid_replay = subparsers.add_parser("hybrid-replay")
    hybrid_replay.add_argument("--semantic-directory", type=Path, required=True)
    hybrid_replay.add_argument("--case-specifications", type=Path, required=True)
    hybrid_replay.add_argument("--output", type=Path)
    hybrid_replay.add_argument("--packet-output-directory", type=Path)

    subparsers.add_parser("print-ruleset-hash")
    return parser


def _utc_now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="microseconds").replace(
        "+00:00", "Z"
    )


def _write(path: Path, encoded: bytes) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_bytes(encoded)


def _analyze(arguments: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    started_at = _utc_now()
    monotonic_start = time.monotonic_ns()
    exit_code = 5
    try:
        result = analyze_manifest_bytes(
            arguments.candidate.read_bytes(),
            repository_path=arguments.repository_path,
        )
        encoded = semantic_result_bytes(result)
        _write(arguments.output, encoded)
        exit_code = result_exit_code(result)
        return exit_code
    finally:
        finished_at = _utc_now()
        duration_ms = max(0, (time.monotonic_ns() - monotonic_start) // 1_000_000)
        envelope = RunEnvelope(
            schema_version=RUN_ENVELOPE_SCHEMA_VERSION,
            analysis_version=ANALYSIS_VERSION,
            operation="analyze-manifest",
            input_path=str(arguments.candidate),
            output_path=str(arguments.output),
            started_at_utc=started_at,
            finished_at_utc=finished_at,
            hostname=socket.gethostname(),
            pid=os.getpid(),
            duration_ms=duration_ms,
            exit_code=exit_code,
        )
        _write(arguments.run_envelope, canonical_json_bytes(envelope))


def _validate(arguments: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    result = validate_result_bytes(arguments.result.read_bytes())
    print(result.semantic_sha256)
    return 0


def _replay(arguments: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    if arguments.runs < 2:
        raise ResultValidationError("replay requires at least two runs")
    candidate_bytes = arguments.candidate.read_bytes()
    results = [
        analyze_manifest_bytes(
            candidate_bytes,
            repository_path=arguments.repository_path,
        )
        for _ in range(arguments.runs)
    ]
    encoded_results = [semantic_result_bytes(result) for result in results]
    if any(encoded != encoded_results[0] for encoded in encoded_results[1:]):
        raise ResultValidationError("replay produced non-identical semantic bytes")
    if arguments.expected is not None:
        expected = arguments.expected.read_bytes()
        validate_result_bytes(expected)
        if expected != encoded_results[0]:
            raise ResultValidationError("replay differs from the expected semantic result")
    if arguments.output is not None:
        _write(arguments.output, encoded_results[0])
    print(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "byte_identical": True,
                "runs": arguments.runs,
                "semantic_sha256": results[0].semantic_sha256,
            },
            sort_keys=True,
            separators=(",", ":"),
        )
    )
    return result_exit_code(results[0])


def _build_review_packet(arguments: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    result = validate_result_bytes(arguments.result.read_bytes())
    packet = build_review_packet(result)
    _write(arguments.output, review_packet_bytes(packet))
    print(packet.review_packet_sha256)
    return 0


def _validate_review_packet(arguments: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    packet = validate_review_packet_bytes(arguments.packet.read_bytes())
    print(packet.review_packet_sha256)
    return 0


def _validate_review_decision(arguments: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    packet = validate_review_packet_bytes(arguments.review_packet.read_bytes())
    decision = validate_review_decision_bytes(arguments.decision.read_bytes(), packet)
    print(decision.review_decision_sha256)
    return 0


def _hybrid_route(arguments: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
    result = validate_result_bytes(arguments.result.read_bytes())
    encoded = canonical_json_bytes(hybrid_route(result))
    if arguments.output is None:
        sys.stdout.buffer.write(encoded)
    else:
        _write(arguments.output, encoded)
    return 0


def _rate(numerator: int, denominator: int) -> str:
    if denominator < 1:
        raise ResultValidationError("hybrid replay requires at least one case")
    scaled = (numerator * 1_000_000 + denominator // 2) // denominator
    return f"{scaled // 1_000_000}.{scaled % 1_000_000:06d}"


def _case_classes(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    try:
        value = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
        raise ResultValidationError("case specifications are not UTF-8 JSON") from error
    if not isinstance(value, dict) or not isinstance(value.get("cases"), list):
        raise ResultValidationError("case specifications must contain a cases array")
    classes: dict[str, str] = {}
    for item in value["cases"]:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            raise ResultValidationError("case specification rows must be objects")
        case_id = item.get("case_id")
        gold_class = item.get("gold_class")
        if (
            not isinstance(case_id, str)
            or not case_id
            or gold_class not in {"POSITIVE", "DIFFICULT_NEGATIVE"}
            or case_id in classes
        ):
            raise ResultValidationError("case specification identity is invalid")
        classes[case_id] = gold_class
    if value.get("case_count") != len(classes):
        raise ResultValidationError("case specification count is inconsistent")
    return classes

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class LedgerState:
    successor_positions_processed: int
    historical_unique_opened_anchors: int
    global_unique_opened_anchors: int
    next_due_position: int
    final_families: int
    reserve_required: int
    final_target: int
    trust_category_counts: tuple[tuple[str, int], ...]
    admitted_repository_groups: tuple[str, ...]
    records_published: int
    global_action: GlobalAction
    administrative_unopened_positions: tuple[int, ...] = ()

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        nonnegative = (
            self.successor_positions_processed,
            self.historical_unique_opened_anchors,
            self.global_unique_opened_anchors,
            self.final_families,
            self.reserve_required,
            self.final_target,
            self.records_published,
        )
        if any(isinstance(item, bool) or item < 0 for item in nonnegative):
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("ledger counts must be nonnegative integers")
        if self.historical_unique_opened_anchors != HISTORICAL_UNIQUE_OPENED_ANCHORS:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("historical unique-opened count is frozen at two")
        if self.next_due_position != self.successor_positions_processed + 1:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("next due position must follow processed count")
        if (
            tuple(sorted(set(self.administrative_unopened_positions)))
            != self.administrative_unopened_positions
            or any(
                isinstance(position, bool)
                or not 1 <= position <= self.successor_positions_processed
                or position in HISTORICAL_REPROCESSED_POSITIONS
                for position in self.administrative_unopened_positions
            )
        ):
            raise ProtocolInvariantError(
                "administrative unopened positions must be unique processed successors"
            )
        newly_openable_positions = set(
            range(1, self.successor_positions_processed + 1)
        ) - HISTORICAL_REPROCESSED_POSITIONS
        expected_global = self.historical_unique_opened_anchors + len(
            newly_openable_positions - set(self.administrative_unopened_positions)
        )
        if self.global_unique_opened_anchors != expected_global:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("global unique-opened accounting is inconsistent")
        if self.global_unique_opened_anchors > MAX_GLOBAL_UNIQUE_OPENED_ANCHORS:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("hard unique-opened-anchor ceiling exceeded")
        if self.reserve_required != REQUIRED_RESERVE_FAMILIES:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("reserve requirement differs from frozen rule")
        if self.final_target != TARGET_FINAL_FAMILIES:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("final target differs from frozen rule")
        if self.records_published != self.successor_positions_processed:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("every processed position requires one durable record")
        if tuple(sorted(self.trust_category_counts)) != self.trust_category_counts:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("trust category counts must be ordered")
        counts = dict(self.trust_category_counts)
        if len(counts) != len(self.trust_category_counts):
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("trust category counts must be unique")
        for category, count in counts.items():
            if category not in TRUST_CATEGORIES or isinstance(count, bool) or count <= 0:
                raise ProtocolInvariantError("trust category count is invalid")
            cap = (
                MAX_OTHER_PREDECLARED
                if category == OTHER_PREDECLARED_CATEGORY
                else MAX_FINAL_FAMILIES_PER_CATEGORY
            )
            if count > cap:
                raise ProtocolInvariantError("trust category cap exceeded")
        if sum(counts.values()) != self.final_families:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("final count and category counts differ")
        if (
            len(set(self.admitted_repository_groups))
            != len(self.admitted_repository_groups)
            or tuple(sorted(self.admitted_repository_groups))
            != self.admitted_repository_groups
            or len(self.admitted_repository_groups) != self.final_families
        ):
        ):
            raise ProtocolInvariantError(
                "one unique repository-independence group is required per final"
            )
        expected_action = evaluate_stopping_rule(
            trust_category_counts=counts,
            admitted_repository_groups=self.admitted_repository_groups,
            global_unique_opened_anchors=self.global_unique_opened_anchors,
        )
        if self.global_action is not expected_action:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("global action is not chain-derived")

    @property
    def trust_categories_represented(self) -> int:
        return sum(
            category in NAMED_TRUST_CATEGORIES for category, _ in self.trust_category_counts
        )


def sha256_bytes(value: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(value).hexdigest()


def sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    return sha256_bytes(path.read_bytes())


def canonical_sha256(value: Any) -> str:
    return sha256_bytes(canonical_json_bytes(value))


def load_json(path: Path) -> Any:
    try:
        return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, UnicodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError(f"cannot parse JSON artifact: {path}") from error


def verify_sha256_sidecar(path: Path, sidecar: Path) -> str:
    digest = sha256_file(path)
    expected = f"{digest}  {path.name}\n"
    try:
        observed = sidecar.read_text(encoding="ascii")
    except (OSError, UnicodeError) as error:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError(f"cannot read SHA-256 sidecar: {sidecar}") from error
    if observed != expected:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError(f"SHA-256 sidecar mismatch: {sidecar}")
    return digest

def evaluate_stopping_rule(
    *,
    trust_category_counts: Mapping[str, int],
    admitted_repository_groups: Sequence[str],
    global_unique_opened_anchors: int,
) -> GlobalAction:
    if isinstance(global_unique_opened_anchors, bool) or not (
        0 <= global_unique_opened_anchors <= MAX_GLOBAL_UNIQUE_OPENED_ANCHORS
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("global unique-opened count is outside the ceiling")
    if len(set(admitted_repository_groups)) != len(admitted_repository_groups):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("repository-independence groups must be unique")
    final_count = 0
    represented = 0
    for category, count in trust_category_counts.items():
        if category not in TRUST_CATEGORIES or isinstance(count, bool) or count <= 0:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("stopping-rule category count is invalid")
        cap = (
            MAX_OTHER_PREDECLARED
            if category == OTHER_PREDECLARED_CATEGORY
            else MAX_FINAL_FAMILIES_PER_CATEGORY
        )
        if count > cap:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("stopping-rule category cap exceeded")
        final_count += count
        represented += category in NAMED_TRUST_CATEGORIES
    if final_count != len(admitted_repository_groups):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("finals and repository groups must be one-to-one")
    if final_count >= TARGET_FINAL_FAMILIES and represented >= MINIMUM_TRUST_CATEGORIES:
        return GlobalAction.STOP_TARGET_REACHED
    if global_unique_opened_anchors >= MAX_GLOBAL_UNIQUE_OPENED_ANCHORS:
        return GlobalAction.HALT_HARD_UNIQUE_ANCHOR_CEILING
    return GlobalAction.CONTINUE


def validate_family_executable_invariants(
    evidence: FamilyExecutableEvidence,
) -> SuccessorProcessingState:
    if not evidence.recipe_semantics_unchanged:
        return SuccessorProcessingState.FAMILY_CONSTRUCTION_FAILED
    expected = (
        evidence.source_predicate == "TRUE"
        and evidence.compatible_predicate == "TRUE"
        and evidence.invalidated_predicate == "FALSE"
        and evidence.functional_reuse == "PASS"
        and evidence.witness_reuse == "TRIGGERED"
        and evidence.functional_safe == "PASS"
        and evidence.witness_safe == "BLOCKED"
        and evidence.isolated_focal_trust_change_count == 1
        and evidence.trust_category in TRUST_CATEGORIES
        and evidence.repository_independence_group is not None
    )
    if not expected:
        return SuccessorProcessingState.FAMILY_VALIDATION_FAILED
    return SuccessorProcessingState.VALIDATED_FAMILY


def evaluate_family_admission(
    evidence: FamilyExecutableEvidence,
    *,
    final_category_counts: Mapping[str, int],
    admitted_repository_groups: Sequence[str],
) -> SuccessorProcessingState:
    validation = validate_family_executable_invariants(evidence)
    if validation is not SuccessorProcessingState.VALIDATED_FAMILY:
        return validation
    category = evidence.trust_category
    group = evidence.repository_independence_group
    assert category is not None and group is not None
    if group in admitted_repository_groups:
        return SuccessorProcessingState.VALIDATED_NOT_ADMITTED_REPOSITORY_GROUP
    cap = (
        MAX_OTHER_PREDECLARED
        if category == OTHER_PREDECLARED_CATEGORY
        else MAX_FINAL_FAMILIES_PER_CATEGORY
    )
    if final_category_counts.get(category, 0) >= cap:
        return SuccessorProcessingState.VALIDATED_NOT_ADMITTED_CATEGORY_CAP
    return SuccessorProcessingState.ADMIT_FINAL


def advance_ledger_position(
    state: LedgerState,
    *,
    queue_position: int,
    processing_state: SuccessorProcessingState | AdministrativeProcessingState,
    admitted_category: str | None = None,
    admitted_repository_group: str | None = None,
) -> LedgerState:
    if state.global_action is not GlobalAction.CONTINUE:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("the ledger is not authorized to continue")
    if queue_position != state.next_due_position:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("successor positions must be processed in queue order")
    if not isinstance(
        processing_state, (SuccessorProcessingState, AdministrativeProcessingState)
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("processing state is outside the frozen vocabulary")
    is_administrative = isinstance(processing_state, AdministrativeProcessingState)
    is_final = processing_state is SuccessorProcessingState.ADMIT_FINAL
    if is_final != (admitted_category is not None and admitted_repository_group is not None):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("final admission requires category and group together")
    counts = dict(state.trust_category_counts)
    groups = set(state.admitted_repository_groups)
    if is_final:
        assert admitted_category is not None and admitted_repository_group is not None
        if admitted_category not in TRUST_CATEGORIES:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("admitted category is outside frozen categories")
        if admitted_repository_group in groups:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("repository-independence group already admitted")
        cap = (
            MAX_OTHER_PREDECLARED
            if admitted_category == OTHER_PREDECLARED_CATEGORY
            else MAX_FINAL_FAMILIES_PER_CATEGORY
        )
        if counts.get(admitted_category, 0) >= cap:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("category cap forbids final admission")
        counts[admitted_category] = counts.get(admitted_category, 0) + 1
        groups.add(admitted_repository_group)
    processed = state.successor_positions_processed + 1
    administrative_positions = set(state.administrative_unopened_positions)
    if is_administrative:
        administrative_positions.add(queue_position)
    global_unique = state.global_unique_opened_anchors + (
        0
        if is_administrative or queue_position in HISTORICAL_REPROCESSED_POSITIONS
        else 1
    )
    action = evaluate_stopping_rule(
        trust_category_counts=counts,
        admitted_repository_groups=tuple(sorted(groups)),
        global_unique_opened_anchors=global_unique,
    )
    return replace(
        state,
        successor_positions_processed=processed,
        global_unique_opened_anchors=global_unique,
        next_due_position=queue_position + 1,
        final_families=state.final_families + int(is_final),
        trust_category_counts=tuple(sorted(counts.items())),
        admitted_repository_groups=tuple(sorted(groups)),
        records_published=state.records_published + 1,
        global_action=action,
        administrative_unopened_positions=tuple(sorted(administrative_positions)),
    )

def select_administrative_processing_state(
    queue_entry: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,
    frozen_repository_anchor_limit: int,
) -> AdministrativeProcessingState | None:
    """Return the sole predeclared administrative terminal state, if present.

    Eligible entries remain on the unchanged scientific path.  Ineligible entries
    fail closed unless their queue fields exactly express the already-frozen
    repository-anchor exclusion; no new administrative exclusion is inferred here.
    """

    if (
        isinstance(frozen_repository_anchor_limit, bool)
        or not isinstance(frozen_repository_anchor_limit, int)
        or frozen_repository_anchor_limit < 1
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("frozen repository anchor limit is invalid")
    inspection_eligible = queue_entry.get("inspection_eligible")
    administrative_code = queue_entry.get("administrative_code")
    if inspection_eligible is True:
        if administrative_code is not None:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError(
                "an inspection-eligible queue entry cannot carry an administrative code"
            )
        return None
    if inspection_eligible is not False:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("queue inspection eligibility must be boolean")
    if administrative_code != (
        AdministrativeProcessingState.ADMIN_REPOSITORY_ANCHOR_LIMIT.value
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError(
            "ineligible queue entry has no supported predeclared administrative state"
        )
    repository_position = queue_entry.get("candidate_position_within_repository")
    if (
        isinstance(repository_position, bool)
        or not isinstance(repository_position, int)
        or repository_position <= frozen_repository_anchor_limit
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError(
            "repository-anchor administrative fields are internally inconsistent"
        )
    return AdministrativeProcessingState.ADMIN_REPOSITORY_ANCHOR_LIMIT


def validate_route_transition(
    *,
    routing_state: HybridRoutingState,
    processing_state: SuccessorProcessingState,
    combined_review_state: ReviewOutcome | None,
) -> None:
    if routing_state is HybridRoutingState.AUTO_MECHANICAL_REJECT:
        if (
            processing_state is not SuccessorProcessingState.AUTO_MECHANICAL_REJECT
            or combined_review_state is not None
        ):
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("mechanical exclusion is the only automatic reject")
        return
    if routing_state is HybridRoutingState.OUT_OF_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED:
        if processing_state is not SuccessorProcessingState.OUT_OF_SCOPE_UNSUPPORTED:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("unsupported scope must remain explicit")
        return
    if routing_state is HybridRoutingState.ANALYSIS_ERROR:
        if processing_state is not SuccessorProcessingState.ANALYSIS_ERROR:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("analysis errors must remain explicit")
        return
    if processing_state is SuccessorProcessingState.AUTO_MECHANICAL_REJECT:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("G2-G8 semantic results cannot auto-reject")
    if routing_state is HybridRoutingState.AUTO_RETAIN_FOR_CONSTRUCTION:
        if combined_review_state is not None:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("automatic retain does not fabricate review authority")
        allowed = {
            SuccessorProcessingState.AUTO_RETAIN_FOR_CONSTRUCTION,

        SuccessorProcessingState.REVIEW_REJECT: ReviewOutcome.REVIEW_REJECT,

        SuccessorProcessingState.REVIEW_RETAIN: ReviewOutcome.REVIEW_RETAIN,

        if combined_review_state is not None:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("pending structured review has no combined outcome")
        return
    required = review_state_by_processing.get(processing_state)
    if required is not None and combined_review_state is not required:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("review processing state and combined decision differ")

        SuccessorProcessingState.FAMILY_CONSTRUCTION_FAILED,
        SuccessorProcessingState.FAMILY_VALIDATION_FAILED,
        SuccessorProcessingState.VALIDATED_FAMILY,
        SuccessorProcessingState.ADMIT_FINAL,
        SuccessorProcessingState.VALIDATED_NOT_ADMITTED_CATEGORY_CAP,
        SuccessorProcessingState.VALIDATED_NOT_ADMITTED_REPOSITORY_GROUP,

def verify_sealed_queue_identity(repository_root: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    queue_path = repository_root / QUEUE_RELATIVE_PATH
    manifest_path = repository_root / QUEUE_MANIFEST_RELATIVE_PATH
    if sha256_file(queue_path) != QUEUE_SHA256:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("sealed queue bytes changed")
    if sha256_file(manifest_path) != QUEUE_MANIFEST_SHA256:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("sealed queue manifest bytes changed")
    manifest = load_json(manifest_path)
    expected = queue_identity()
    observed = {
        "queue_path": str(QUEUE_RELATIVE_PATH),
        "queue_sha256": manifest.get("queue_artifact", {}).get("sha256"),
        "queue_manifest_path": str(QUEUE_MANIFEST_RELATIVE_PATH),
        "queue_manifest_sha256": QUEUE_MANIFEST_SHA256,
        "input_identity_set_sha256": manifest.get("input_identity_set_sha256"),
        "candidate_count": manifest.get("candidate_count"),
        "repository_count": manifest.get("repository_count"),
    }
    if observed != expected:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("sealed queue manifest identity changed")
    return expected

def ledger_state_from_document(document: Mapping[str, Any]) -> LedgerState:
    state = document.get("state")
    if not isinstance(state, Mapping):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("ledger state must be an object")
    try:
        return LedgerState(
            successor_positions_processed=state["successor_positions_processed"],
            historical_unique_opened_anchors=state[
                "historical_unique_opened_anchors"
            ],
            global_unique_opened_anchors=state["global_unique_opened_anchors"],
            next_due_position=state["next_due_position"],
            final_families=state["FINAL"],
            reserve_required=state["RESERVE_REQUIRED"],
            final_target=state["FINAL_TARGET"],
            trust_category_counts=tuple(
                (item["category"], item["final_count"])
                for item in state["trust_category_counts"]
            ),
            admitted_repository_groups=tuple(state["admitted_repository_groups"]),
            records_published=state["records_published"],
            global_action=GlobalAction(state["global_action"]),
            administrative_unopened_positions=tuple(
                state.get("administrative_unopened_positions", ())
            ),
        )
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as error:
        if isinstance(error, ProtocolInvariantError):
            raise
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("ledger state fields are invalid") from error


def _record_paths_for_count(run_id: str, count: int) -> list[str]:
    if _SHA256.fullmatch(run_id) is None:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("ledger run identity is invalid")
    run_root = PurePosixPath("benchmark-selection/screening/runs/v0.2.0") / (
        f"run-{run_id}"
    )
    return [
        str(run_root / "records" / f"{position:08d}.json")
        for position in range(1, count + 1)
    ]


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class AdministrativePublication:
    record_path: str
    record: dict[str, Any]
    ledger_document: dict[str, Any]

    def record_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        return canonical_json_bytes(self.record) + b"\n"

    def ledger_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        return (
            json.dumps(self.ledger_document, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n"
        ).encode("utf-8")

    def ledger_sidecar_bytes(self) -> bytes:
        return f"{sha256_bytes(self.ledger_bytes())}  ledger.json\n".encode("ascii")


def prepare_administrative_publication(
    ledger_document: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,
    queue_entry: Mapping[str, Any],
    frozen_repository_anchor_limit: int,
    previous_record_sha256: str | None,
) -> AdministrativePublication:
    """Prepare, but do not write, one queue-derived administrative publication."""

    state = ledger_state_from_document(ledger_document)
    if (
        ledger_document.get("schema")
        not in {"candidate-screening-successor-ledger-v0.2.0", AMENDED_LEDGER_SCHEMA}
        or ledger_document.get("protocol_version") != PROTOCOL_VERSION
        or ledger_document.get("screening_method_version") != SCREENING_METHOD_VERSION
        or ledger_document.get("queue_identity") != queue_identity()
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("successor ledger frozen identity differs")
    run_id = ledger_document.get("run_id")
    authorization = ledger_document.get("production_authorization_sha256")
    if (
        not isinstance(run_id, str)
        or run_id != authorization
        or _SHA256.fullmatch(run_id) is None
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("ledger production authorization differs")
    record_paths = ledger_document.get("record_paths")
    if (
        not isinstance(record_paths, list)
        or record_paths != _record_paths_for_count(run_id, state.records_published)
        or ledger_document.get("records_published") != state.records_published
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("ledger record publication sequence differs")
    queue_position = queue_entry.get("queue_position")
    if queue_position != state.next_due_position:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("successor positions must be processed in queue order")
    if state.records_published == 0:
        if previous_record_sha256 is not None:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError("first record cannot have a predecessor")
    elif (
        not isinstance(previous_record_sha256, str)
        or _SHA256.fullmatch(previous_record_sha256) is None
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("published successor requires its predecessor hash")
    processing_state = select_administrative_processing_state(
        queue_entry,
        frozen_repository_anchor_limit=frozen_repository_anchor_limit,
    )
    if processing_state is None:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError(
            "inspection-eligible entries require the unchanged scientific controller"
        )
    next_state = advance_ledger_position(
        state,
        queue_position=queue_position,
        processing_state=processing_state,
    )
    queue_state = {
        "inspection_eligible": queue_entry["inspection_eligible"],
        "administrative_code": queue_entry["administrative_code"],
        "candidate_position_within_repository": queue_entry[
            "candidate_position_within_repository"
        ],
        "frozen_repository_anchor_limit": frozen_repository_anchor_limit,
    }
    record: dict[str, Any] = {
        "schema": ADMINISTRATIVE_RECORD_SCHEMA,
        "protocol_version": PROTOCOL_VERSION,
        "screening_method_version": SCREENING_METHOD_VERSION,
        "operational_amendment": administrative_amendment_identity(),
        "queue_position": queue_position,
        "queue_identity": queue_identity(),
        "queue_entry_sha256": canonical_sha256(queue_entry),
        "administrative": True,
        "scientifically_opened": False,
        "administrative_reason": processing_state.value,
        "queue_administrative_state": queue_state,
        "source_checkout_performed": False,
        "base_repair_resolution_performed": False,
        "candidate_source_inspection_performed": False,
        "tptm_run": False,
        "reviewer_a": False,
        "reviewer_b": False,
        "family_construction": False,
        "executable_validation": False,
        "FINAL": False,
        "processing_state": processing_state.value,
        "stopping_rule_state_after_publication": ledger_state_document(next_state),
        "previous_record_sha256": previous_record_sha256,
        "record_sha256": "0" * 64,
    }
    record["record_sha256"] = semantic_record_hash(record)
    validate_administrative_terminal_record(record)
    updated_ledger = deepcopy(dict(ledger_document))
    updated_ledger["schema"] = AMENDED_LEDGER_SCHEMA
    updated_ledger["operational_amendment"] = administrative_amendment_identity()
    updated_ledger["state"] = ledger_state_document(next_state)
    record_path = _record_paths_for_count(run_id, next_state.records_published)[-1]
    updated_ledger["record_paths"] = [*record_paths, record_path]
    updated_ledger["records_published"] = next_state.records_published
    return AdministrativePublication(
        record_path=record_path,
        record=record,
        ledger_document=updated_ledger,
    )

def semantic_record_hash(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
    payload = {key: value for key, value in record.items() if key != "record_sha256"}
    return canonical_sha256(payload)


def validate_successor_record(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    required = {
        "schema",
        "protocol_version",
        "screening_method_version",
        "candidate_id",
        "queue_position",
        "queue_identity",
        "base_candidate_evidence_identity",
        "head_candidate_evidence_identity",
        "tptm_release_commit",
        "ruleset_sha256",
        "configuration_sha256",
        "candidate_result_schema_sha256",
        "review_packet_schema_sha256",
        "review_decision_schema_sha256",
        "semantic_result_sha256",
        "hybrid_routing_state",
        "reviewer_a_decision_sha256",
        "reviewer_b_decision_sha256",
        "combined_review_state",
        "family_recipe_sha256",
        "family_construction_state",
        "family_executable_validation_state",
        "admission_state",
        "processing_state",
        "repository_independence_group",
        "trust_category",
        "stopping_rule_state_after_publication",
        "previous_record_sha256",
        "record_sha256",
    }
    if set(record) != required:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("successor record fields are not exact")
    if record["schema"] != "candidate-screening-record-v0.2.0":
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("successor record schema identity differs")
    if (
        not isinstance(record["candidate_id"], str)
        or _CANDIDATE_ID.fullmatch(record["candidate_id"]) is None
        or isinstance(record["queue_position"], bool)
        or not isinstance(record["queue_position"], int)
        or not 1 <= record["queue_position"] <= SEALED_CANDIDATE_COUNT
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("successor record candidate binding is invalid")
    if (
        record["protocol_version"] != PROTOCOL_VERSION
        or record["screening_method_version"] != SCREENING_METHOD_VERSION
        or record["tptm_release_commit"] != VALIDATED_TPTM_COMMIT
        or record["ruleset_sha256"] != RULESET_SHA256
        or record["configuration_sha256"] != CONFIGURATION_SHA256
        or record["candidate_result_schema_sha256"]
        != CANDIDATE_RESULT_SCHEMA_SHA256
        or record["review_packet_schema_sha256"] != REVIEW_PACKET_SCHEMA_SHA256
        or record["review_decision_schema_sha256"] != REVIEW_DECISION_SCHEMA_SHA256
        or record["queue_identity"] != queue_identity()
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("successor record frozen identity differs")
    for key in (
        "base_candidate_evidence_identity",
        "head_candidate_evidence_identity",
        "semantic_result_sha256",
        "record_sha256",
    ):
        if not isinstance(record[key], str) or _SHA256.fullmatch(record[key]) is None:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError(f"{key} must be a SHA-256")
    for key in (
        "reviewer_a_decision_sha256",
        "reviewer_b_decision_sha256",
        "family_recipe_sha256",
        "previous_record_sha256",
    ):
        if record[key] is not None and (
            not isinstance(record[key], str) or _SHA256.fullmatch(record[key]) is None
        ):
            raise ProtocolInvariantError(f"{key} must be a SHA-256 or null")
    if semantic_record_hash(record) != record["record_sha256"]:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("successor record semantic hash differs")
    try:
        route = HybridRoutingState(record["hybrid_routing_state"])
        processing = SuccessorProcessingState(record["processing_state"])
        combined = (
            None
            if record["combined_review_state"] is None
            else ReviewOutcome(record["combined_review_state"])
        )
    except ValueError as error:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("record state vocabulary differs") from error
    validate_route_transition(
        routing_state=route,
        processing_state=processing,
        combined_review_state=combined,
    )


def validate_administrative_terminal_record(record: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    required = {
        "schema",
        "protocol_version",
        "screening_method_version",
        "operational_amendment",
        "queue_position",
        "queue_identity",
        "queue_entry_sha256",
        "administrative",
        "scientifically_opened",
        "administrative_reason",
        "queue_administrative_state",
        "source_checkout_performed",
        "base_repair_resolution_performed",
        "candidate_source_inspection_performed",
        "tptm_run",
        "reviewer_a",
        "reviewer_b",
        "family_construction",
        "executable_validation",
        "FINAL",
        "processing_state",
        "stopping_rule_state_after_publication",
        "previous_record_sha256",
        "record_sha256",
    }
    if set(record) != required:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("administrative terminal record fields are not exact")
    if (
        record["schema"] != ADMINISTRATIVE_RECORD_SCHEMA
        or record["protocol_version"] != PROTOCOL_VERSION
        or record["screening_method_version"] != SCREENING_METHOD_VERSION
        or record["operational_amendment"] != administrative_amendment_identity()
        or record["queue_identity"] != queue_identity()
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("administrative terminal frozen identity differs")
    queue_position = record["queue_position"]
    if (
        isinstance(queue_position, bool)
        or not isinstance(queue_position, int)
        or not 1 <= queue_position <= SEALED_CANDIDATE_COUNT
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("administrative queue position is invalid")
    for key in ("queue_entry_sha256", "record_sha256"):
        if not isinstance(record[key], str) or _SHA256.fullmatch(record[key]) is None:
            raise ProtocolInvariantError(f"{key} must be a SHA-256")
    previous = record["previous_record_sha256"]
    if previous is not None and (
        not isinstance(previous, str) or _SHA256.fullmatch(previous) is None
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("previous_record_sha256 must be a SHA-256 or null")
    required_false = {
        "scientifically_opened",
        "source_checkout_performed",
        "base_repair_resolution_performed",
        "candidate_source_inspection_performed",
        "tptm_run",
        "reviewer_a",
        "reviewer_b",
        "family_construction",
        "executable_validation",
        "FINAL",
    }
    if record["administrative"] is not True or any(
        record[key] is not False for key in required_false
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError(
            "administrative terminal record cannot claim scientific processing"
        )
    expected_reason = (
        AdministrativeProcessingState.ADMIN_REPOSITORY_ANCHOR_LIMIT.value
    )
    if (
        record["administrative_reason"] != expected_reason
        or record["processing_state"] != expected_reason
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("administrative terminal reason differs")
    queue_state = record["queue_administrative_state"]
    if not isinstance(queue_state, Mapping) or set(queue_state) != {
        "inspection_eligible",
        "administrative_code",
        "candidate_position_within_repository",
        "frozen_repository_anchor_limit",
    }:
        raise ProtocolInvariantError("queue administrative state fields are not exact")
    selected = select_administrative_processing_state(
        queue_state,
        frozen_repository_anchor_limit=queue_state["frozen_repository_anchor_limit"],
    )

        raise ProtocolInvariantError("queue state and administrative reason differ")
    stopping_state = ledger_state_from_document(
        {"state": record["stopping_rule_state_after_publication"]}
    )
    if (
        stopping_state.next_due_position != queue_position + 1
        or queue_position not in stopping_state.administrative_unopened_positions
    ):
        raise ProtocolInvariantError(
            "administrative record stopping state is inconsistent"
        )

def ledger_state_document(state: LedgerState) -> dict[str, Any]:
    document: dict[str, Any] = {
        "successor_positions_processed": state.successor_positions_processed,
        "historical_unique_opened_anchors": state.historical_unique_opened_anchors,
        "global_unique_opened_anchors": state.global_unique_opened_anchors,
        "next_due_position": state.next_due_position,
        "FINAL": state.final_families,
        "RESERVE_REQUIRED": state.reserve_required,
        "FINAL_TARGET": state.final_target,
        "trust_categories_represented": state.trust_categories_represented,
        "trust_category_counts": [
            {"category": category, "final_count": count}
            for category, count in state.trust_category_counts
        ],
        "admitted_repository_groups": list(state.admitted_repository_groups),
        "records_published": state.records_published,
        "global_action": state.global_action.value,
    }
    if state.administrative_unopened_positions:
        document["administrative_unopened_positions"] = list(
            state.administrative_unopened_positions
        )
    return document

import pytest
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By
from selenium.webdriver.support.ui import WebDriverWait, Select
from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC
from selenium.webdriver.common.alert import Alert

BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:5000"
TEST_USERNAME = "user1"
TEST_PASSWORD = "123"
SAMPLE_IMAGE_PATH = os.path.abspath("tests/Funny_dogs_2.jpg")

def dismiss_any_alert(driver, timeout=3):
    """Dismiss any alert that may be present."""
    try:
        WebDriverWait(driver, timeout).until(EC.alert_is_present())
        Alert(driver).accept()
    except Exception:
        pass


def safe_get(driver, url):
    """Navigate to a URL and dismiss any unexpected alerts."""
    driver.get(url)
    dismiss_any_alert(driver)


@pytest.fixture
def driver():
    """Set up a headless Edge browser for each test."""
    options = webdriver.EdgeOptions()
    options.add_argument("--headless")
    options.add_argument("--no-sandbox")
    options.add_argument("--disable-dev-shm-usage")
    options.add_argument("--window-size=1920,1080")  # important for interactability

    driver = webdriver.Edge(options=options)
    driver.implicitly_wait(5)
    yield driver
    driver.quit()


def login(driver):
    """Helper function to log in the test user."""
    driver.get(f"{BASE_URL}/login.html")

    WebDriverWait(driver, 5).until(
        EC.visibility_of_element_located((By.ID, "login-username"))
    )

    driver.find_element(By.ID, "login-username").send_keys(TEST_USERNAME)
    driver.find_element(By.ID, "login-password").send_keys(TEST_PASSWORD)
    driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR, "#login-form button[type='submit']").click()

    # Handle the "Logged in successfully" alert
    try:
        WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(EC.alert_is_present())
        Alert(driver).accept()
    except Exception:
        pass

    # Wait until we are no longer on the login page
    WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(
        lambda d: "login" not in d.current_url
    )


def fill_checkin_form(driver, include_location=True):
    """Helper function to fill in the check-in form."""
    WebDriverWait(driver, 5).until(
        EC.visibility_of_element_located((By.ID, "title"))
    )

    # Fill in place name
    driver.find_element(By.ID, "place-name").send_keys("Test Place Name")

    # Fill in the title
    driver.find_element(By.ID, "title").send_keys("Test Checkin Place")

    # Select a category
